IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: To conduct independent, high-quality research to improve learning for each and every child.
IRS990.MissionDesc: The Learning Policy Institute (LPI) conducts and disseminates independent, high-quality research to improve learning for all children. A nonprofit, nonpartisan organization, LPI connects policymakers and stakeholders at the local, state, and federal levels with the evidence and strategies needed to strengthen the education system from preschool through college and career.
IRS990.Desc: Early Childhood Education. LPI research informed policymakers' efforts to provide universal access to high-quality early learning. Reports examined California's progress toward universal prekindergarten, integration in early childhood education, and coaching as a strategy for strengthening the early learning workforce. Educator Quality. LPI developed tools to assess the cost of teacher turnover and the extent of teacher shortages in each state. LPI published reports examining successful teacher residencies, state and federal policies to support residencies, and how teacher preparation predicts teacher performance assessment results. In the area of school leadership, LPI conducted research on state approaches to developing educational leaders, preparing leaders for deeper learning, and the California School Leadership Academy. Equitable Resources and Access. LPI partnered with the National Conference of State Legislatures to support adequate and equitable state school finance reform. LPI also published briefs on the progress of English Learners in California and the costs of universal school vouchers. Whole Child Education. LPI authored a comprehensive guide on redesigning high schools and a framework for creating community schools as part of a new Center for School and System Redesign. LPI also published a report on how community schools can reduce chronic absenteeism and a series of analyses of statewide efforts to support community schools in New Mexico.

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Income Taxes - The Institute is exempt from income taxes under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. The Institute has also received recognition of its exempt status from California and Washington D.C. The Institute has applied the accounting principles related to accounting for uncertainty in income taxes and has determined that there is no material impact on the financial statements. With some exceptions, the Institute is no longer subject to U.S. federal and state income tax examinations by tax authorities for years prior to 2020.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Form 990 was prepared by a Certified Public Accountant. The prepared Form 990 was forwarded to the Chief Financial and Administrative Officer for review. Following the review by the CFAO, the Form 990 was forwarded to the management team and to all members of the governing Board prior to filing.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Each Member of the Board of Directors is required to complete a conflict of interest form. Those forms are reviewed by the Board Chair and any perceived or actual conflicts of interest are addressed.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 15
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Organization has adopted a policy with regard to establishing the compensation of the CEO and CFAO that fulfills the requirements for invoking the rebuttable presumption of reasonableness under Treas. Regs. 53.4958-6. Pursuant to that policy, the process for determining the compensation of the Organization's CEO and CFAO included a review and approval by independent persons, a review of comparable compensation data and contemporaneous substantiation of the deliberation and decision making process. The compensation of the other members of the management team was established by the CEO based upon the compensation earned by persons performing like services for like organizations.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section C, line 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Institute's Form 990 is available upon request. The Institute's governing documents, conflict of interest policy, and financial statements are available as required by the State of California and the federal government.
The process of the Audit Committee has not changed from the prior year.
